briefdescription.para: Reproducing kernel (RK) approximation with explicit (direct) shape function gradients.

detaileddescription.para: The shape function of node $ A $ is the kernel $ \phi_A $ (KernelFunction) multiplied by a correction function, \[ \Psi_A(\boldsymbol{x}) = \boldsymbol{H}^T(\boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_A)\, \boldsymbol{b}(\boldsymbol{x})\, \phi_A(\boldsymbol{x}), \] where $ \boldsymbol{H} $ is the vector of all monomials up to the completeness order $ n $ (Math::computeMonomialBasis(), first entry $ 1 $) evaluated at the shifted coordinates $ \boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_A $. The coefficient vector $ \boldsymbol{b} $ solves \[ \boldsymbol{M}(\boldsymbol{x})\, \boldsymbol{b}(\boldsymbol{x}) = \boldsymbol{H}_0, \qquad \boldsymbol{M}(\boldsymbol{x}) = \sum_{B} \boldsymbol{H}(\boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_B)\, \boldsymbol{H}^T(\boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_B)\, \phi_B(\boldsymbol{x}), \qquad \boldsymbol{H}_0 = \boldsymbol{H}(\boldsymbol{0}) = [1, 0, \dots, 0]^T, \] with the moment matrix $ \boldsymbol{M} $ summed over the kernels covering $ \boldsymbol{x} $. This enforces the reproducing conditions $ \sum_A \Psi_A(\boldsymbol{x})\, (\boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_A)^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} = \delta_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}\boldsymbol{0}} $, or equivalently $ \sum_A \Psi_A(\boldsymbol{x})\, \boldsymbol{x}_A^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} = \boldsymbol{x}^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} $, for all multi-indices $ |\boldsymbol{\alpha}| \le n $; in particular, the shape functions form a partition of unity. The continuity of $ \Psi_A $ is that of the kernels.

The gradients are the exact derivatives of $ \Psi_A $ (product rule), \[ \Psi_{A,i} = \left( \boldsymbol{b}_{,i}^T \boldsymbol{H} + \boldsymbol{b}^T \boldsymbol{H}_{,i} \right) \phi_A + \boldsymbol{b}^T \boldsymbol{H}\, \phi_{A,i}, \qquad \boldsymbol{b}_{,i} = -\boldsymbol{M}^{-1} \boldsymbol{M}_{,i}\, \boldsymbol{b}, \qquad \boldsymbol{M}_{,i} = \sum_B \left( \boldsymbol{H}_{,i} \boldsymbol{H}^T + \boldsymbol{H} \boldsymbol{H}_{,i}^T \right) \phi_B + \boldsymbol{H} \boldsymbol{H}^T \phi_{B,i}, \] with $ (\bullet)_{,i} = \partial (\bullet) / \partial x_i $ and $ \boldsymbol{H} $ evaluated at $ \boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_A $ (resp. $ \boldsymbol{x} - \boldsymbol{x}_B $). The linear systems are solved with a column-pivoting Householder QR decomposition of $ \boldsymbol{M} $, which is computed once per evaluation point.

If fewer kernels cover $ \boldsymbol{x} $ than the basis has entries, $ \boldsymbol{M} $ is singular; the completeness order is then reduced for this evaluation point (getCorrectedCompletenessOrder()).
See ReproducingKernelApproximationImplicit for the variant with implicit gradients.
